messages:
Mei (Support L2): FYI escalation from FinEdge — SSO started failing right after they rotated IdP signing cert overnight. They see login loop and errors in our logs: "Missing NameID" and some XML signature verification failures. Customer says their IdP metadata already contains old+new certs.

James (FinEdge - customer): @Mei yeah we rotated via our IdP (Onelogin) and we did include the new cert in the metadata upload. Login worked once then started looping after a few attempts. Hope you can help, this is blocking all users. :grimacing:

Mei (Support L2): Thanks @James. We captured SAML traces from our frontend. Notably RelayState is present in the POST from the SP but after our ALB and Nginx the ACS receives the request without RelayState (or it's empty). Logs show `POST /sso/acs` 200 then redirect back to idp. Repro: user clicks SSO → IdP redirects POST to https://app.finedge.com/sso/acs (with RelayState) → our server responds with redirect to /login?sso_error=missing_nameid → browser goes back to IdP.

Alex (Auth Eng): Can you paste the raw POST body we got and the SAMLResponse decode? Also which exact IdP metadata XML they uploaded (entityID + KeyDescriptor blocks)? Sometimes ordering/whitespace in metadata causes XML parser to pick an unexpected cert.

Mei (Support L2): Pasted obfuscated SAMLRequest/Response and a stripped stack here: ```
SAMLResponse: <samlp:Response ...>...<saml:Assertion>...<saml:Subject><saml:NameID>...</saml:NameID>...</saml:Assertion></samlp:Response>
Our log snippet: 
[2026-10-22T07:12:11Z] acs POST from 54.88.12.23 - RelayState: ""
[2026-10-22T07:12:11Z] saml: verify signature failed: expected public key id=sha1:XYZ but no match
[2026-10-22T07:12:11Z] session create failed: missing_nameid
```

Priya (Customer Success): Also seeing notes in the customer's IdP UI that there were two cert entries (old and new) for a short overlap. They uploaded metadata immediately after rotation. Could be a cert chain/PKCS7 formatting issue.

Devon (Infra): Quick hypothesis: our ALB/nginx strip or normalize `RelayState` when semicolons/encoding present in the POST target or when `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` + TLS renegotiation happens. There was a bug last year where multi-part POST to `/sso/acs;jsessionid=...` caused query param munging. Could be related if their IdP included extra path segments or url-encoded characters.

Alex (Auth Eng): Two threads to investigate in parallel: cert resolution and RelayState transport. For certs — our SAML validator picks the first KeyInfo certificate that matches signature params. If the IdP metadata contains multiple <KeyDescriptor use="signing"> entries, order matters since our code currently picks first valid matching cert by index before checking full chain. If the IdP uploaded certs in reverse chronological order we might be verifying with the stale cert.

SAML-bot: Automated hint: If the IdP provides idp_metadata_url we can fetch and attempt to validate signatures against all certs in metadata. Use `saml-parse --validate --all-certs` to reproduce locally.

Alex (Auth Eng): Mei — can you run this minimal local repro on the trace file we captured? ```
# decode SAMLResponse base64 -> file.xml
python -c "import base64,sys;print(base64.b64decode(open('saml.b64','rb').read()))" > resp.xml
# run validation (internal tool)
/srv/tools/saml-parse --input resp.xml --metadata finedge-idp.xml --validate --verbose --all-certs
```

Mei (Support L2): Ran that. Output: ```
validation: candidate certs found: 2
cert[0] thumbprint=AB:CD:01 use=signing not matching signature keyinfo
cert[1] thumbprint=FE:DC:99 matches signature but chain missing
verification: signature verification succeeded with cert[1]
post-assertion: NameID present -> but frontend before we process shows RelayState empty
```

James (FinEdge - customer): Interesting — so you see the signature verified with the new cert? So why do users still loop?

Alex (Auth Eng): That suggests two separate issues: signature is okay once we pick right cert, but RelayState loss causes our session lookup to fail (we key session by RelayState token). If RelayState missing we treat as invalid auth and redirect. So why RelayState disappears after ALB/nginx?

Devon (Infra): Checked ingress logs — the ALB rewrites `Location` headers and can drop path params. More importantly, older Nginx config had `underscores_in_headers` and `ignore_invalid_headers` defaults that can surface with weird RelayState encoding (e.g., bytes like `+` vs `%2B`). Could be a double-encoding issue: IdP posts RelayState urlencoded then our TLS edge decodes and re-encodes, changing `+` to space. Browsers sometimes substitute.

Priya (Customer Success): Customer says they definitely see RelayState in the POST from the IdP (they forwarded the raw POST body). Their RelayState token contains a `.` and `+` chars (base64url variant). Suggest short-term workaround: configure the SP to accept RelayState from query param fallback (some IdPs send RelayState in URL when POST fails). We can also tolerate missing RelayState if there's a pending temporary session cookie.

Alex (Auth Eng): Proposed immediate steps: 1) update ACS endpoint to accept RelayState in both POST body and query param (add tolerant parsing). 2) add retry for verification using all certs in metadata rather than first-match (hotfix). 3) ask customer to re-upload metadata ensuring new cert is first (as temporary mitigation). 4) check ALB/nginx for URL normalization edgecases and enable a debug trace on a canary host.

Mei (Support L2): I pushed a canary change to the ACS pod to read RelayState from both POST and query and added extra logging (rollout to canary=5%). Canary logs show RelayState intact in the pod but a few upstream requests still show empty — consistent with ALB stripping.

Devon (Infra): Spun up an ALB debug with header logging. Found requests from Onelogin IPs with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` where body contains `RelayState=` but our ALB logged body as truncated when `Content-Length` header duplicated. There's a known AWS ALB bug when header appears twice in the request from some IdPs' proxy chain. Raising a ticket with AWS now.

Alex (Auth Eng): Meanwhile I'll prepare the hotfix to try all certs. Mei can you capture one failing full trace (raw TCP) from the ALB -> nginx chain and DM me.

Mei (Support L2): Captured and sent to Alex. Also asked customer to temporarily set RelayState to a shorter url-safe token (replace `+` with `-`) and re-test. James will try that in 20m.

James (FinEdge - customer): Tested with url-safe token — login succeeded for 2/2 users. Looks promising. We'll keep testing. Thanks team. :tada:

Priya (Customer Success): Next actions & owners: 
- Alex: prepare hotfix to iterate certs in metadata and deploy canary (ETA 2h).
- Devon: escalate ALB header duplication bug to AWS and add WAF rule to reject duplicated Content-Length for now (ETA 1h).
- Mei: keep canary logs and collect failing traces (ETA ongoing).
- James: confirm full org test after 1h and report.

Alex (Auth Eng): Quick note for postmortem: recommend we treat RelayState tokens as opaque url-safe base64 (RFC4648 url) and document in SP integration guide. Also update metadata ingestion to prefer `use="signing"` and verify against all KeyDescriptor entries on rotate.

SAML-bot: PM reminder: create a postmortem ticket and tag with `sso-cert-rotation` `relaystate-encoding` `aws-alb`.
